_doc: DOC walking and tramping tracks (generated by tools/trails/goal_walks.py from the Department of Conservation's open data, CC-BY 4.0, and the Copernicus DEM; never edit by hand).

trails.name: Camp Creek Route
trails.why: A backcountry route to Camp Creek Hut with the option of following a ridge to the summit of Mount Alexander.

trails.name: Waiorongomai Low Level Loop Track
trails.why: A family-friendly loop walk in the Waiorongomai Valley, past historic goldmining sites.

trails.name: Gold Creek Ridge Track
trails.why: This track follows a long gentle ridge to the Gold Creek Hut.

trails.name: Mutton Creek Track
trails.why: This track links the lower sections of the West and East Manuherikia 4WD Tracks.

trails.name: Klondyke Valley Route
trails.why: This route leads up the valley to a tussock basin enclosed by steep granite cliffs.

trails.name: Dusky Track - Kintail Hut to Loch Maree Hut
trails.why: This difficult tramping track between Lake Hauroko and Lake Manapouri offers huge lakes, gushing rivers, vast forested valleys and lots of mud for experienced and well equipped trampers.

trails.name: Last Creek Track
trails.why: An access track leading to the Rock and Pillar Conservation Area.

trails.name: Ngapuketurua Track
trails.why: This track begins on the Kiko Loop and continues as far as the park boundary on the slopes of Mt Ngapuketurua.

trails.name: Sefton Ridge Track
trails.why: The short but challenging Sefton RidgeTrack in the Kaitake Range can be linked with the Waimoku Track to make a loop.

trails.name: Falls Creek Route
trails.why: A challenging tramping route from the Milford Road into the Falls Creek valley, surrounded by impressive Fiordland mountains.

trails.name: Brewster Track
trails.why: The track starts on State Highway 6, crosses the unbridged Haast River, and climbs steadily through beech forest to the bush line.

trails.name: Dry Acheron Track
trails.why: Access to Dry Acheron Stream and the two covenant areas is provided courtesy of the Dry Acheron and Big Ben station owners.

trails.name: Fenceline Walk Track
trails.why: An easy walking track near Ōtaki. This track is part of Te Araroa Trail.

trails.name: Deadmans Route
trails.why: This challenging tramping route from the Hollyford Road climbs the slope to meet the Routeburn Track near Harris Saddle.

trails.name: The Luge Track
trails.why: This track links the Broken River and Craigieburn valleys, via Lyndon Saddle.

trails.name: Black Hill Track
trails.why: Walk to Black Hill Hut on one of these tracks or combine them to make a circuit.

trails.name: Dusky Track - Upper Spey Hut to Kintail Hut
trails.why: This difficult tramping track between Lake Hauroko and Lake Manapouri offers huge lakes, gushing rivers, vast forested valleys and lots of mud for experienced and well equipped trampers.

trails.name: Gold Creek Loop
trails.why: This easy mountain bike track can be accessed from the Canaan Downs car park.

trails.name: Longview/Makaretu Hut Track - Longview Hut
trails.why: A spectacular walk with panoramic views over the Hawke's Bay on a clear day.

trails.name: Lake Gault Track
trails.why: A gradual climb on a historical tramping track through ancient podocarp forest provides panoramic views of Aoraki /Mount Cook.

trails.name: Pukeatua Track
trails.why: Pukeatua Track connects Otaki Forks to Mangaone South Road. This track is part of Te Araroa Trail.

trails.name: Masters Shelter -Golden Crown Ridge Track
trails.why: The Golden Crown Ridge Track begins behind Masters Shelter. The 2-3 hour walk climbs around a series of rocky knolls before continuing steeply upwards through beech forest to the top of the range.

trails.name: Nardoo Creek Route
trails.why: This route provides access to Nardoo Hut and remotes tops in the area.

trails.name: Hope/Kiwi - 3 Mile Stream Hut Track
trails.why: The track goes from the Hurunui swing bridge to Windy Point, and on to Hope Kiwi Lodge. This track is part of Te Araroa Trail.

trails.name: Whirinaki Waterfall Loop Track
trails.why: On the Whirinaki Waterfall Loop Track you'll follow the Whirinaki River as it flows through podocarp forest.

trails.name: Parks Peak Hut to Yeomans Track
trails.why: This challenging track gives access to Parks Peak Hut and various parts of the north and central Ruahine Range.

trails.name: Stanley River Track
trails.why: This marked route links Charlies Saddle to Stanley Vale Hut in the St James Conservation Area.

trails.name: York Road Loop Track
trails.why: Explore the remnants of the old Egmont Branch railway quarry complex while walking through native forest.

trails.name: Homes Ridge Track
trails.why: This track can be used to access Stanfield Hut and makes for a lovely day walk.

trails.name: French Ridge Track
trails.why: French Ridge Track is a steep and technical alpine hike in Mt Aspiring National Park. It leads to French Ridge Hut at 1480 m.

trails.name: Mount French Track
trails.why: Climb to the top of Mount French for spectacular views of Lake Brunner and the Southern Alps.

trails.name: Globe Hill Track
trails.why: This track is for both trampers and mountain bikers. It connects the Reefton township with the Globe Progress Mine site.

trails.name: Te Rereatukahia Hut Track
trails.why: Grass clearings and an old fence are a legacy of days gone by when this section was highly modified by burning and farming.

trails.name: Okiwi Bay Seaward Valley Track
trails.why: Walk or mountain bike through varied vegetation and enjoy ocean views.

trails.name: Pakihi Track - Motu Road to Pakihi Hut
trails.why: Pakihi Walk climbs through kamahi and rimu forest to a platform lookout.

trails.name: Pupu Hydro Walkway
trails.why: Retracing an old gold-mining water race, this short walk passes through forest of young beech and rimu to mature podocarps - it's good for children but be sure to supervise them.

trails.name: Mistletoe Track
trails.why: This track climbs from the Craigieburn picnic area to Lyndon Saddle

trails.name: Saddle Ridge Track
trails.why: A rough and steep track that links the West and East Manuherikia 4WD Tracks. There are spectacular views of Aoraki Mount Cook.

trails.name: Wakamarina Track
trails.why: Follow in the footsteps of old goldminers on the Wakamarina Track to cross the Richmond Range from the Wairau Valley to the Wakamarina Valley.

trails.name: East Holdsworth Track
trails.why: This track connects Atiwhakatu Valley with the alpine tops near Mt Holsworth. It is a more challenging track than the main track to Mt Holdsworth via Powell Hut.

trails.name: Mount Shrimpton Track
trails.why: A good, steep bush walk to the uplands of the McKerrow Range. Great views of the Makarora Valley below and the alps beyond.

trails.name: Tuahu Track
trails.why: This is an east-west crossing of the Kaimai Ranges used since the 1890s linking Katikati and Te Aroha.

trails.name: Waitahu-Murray Connecting Track
trails.why: This historic pack track links Murray Creek with Waitahu valley. It's part of a popular mountain biking circuit.

trails.name: Makarora Track
trails.why: Follow this challenging backcountry tramping track to the 4-bunk Makarora Hut, passing Stewart Falls along the way.

trails.name: Berwen Track
trails.why: This track crosses private farmland and links the East Manuherikia 4WD Track with the Hawkdun Range.

trails.name: Pukaka Valley Track
trails.why: This forested valley is part of Mt Robertson Scenic Reserve and provides good tramping and hunting opportunities and gives alternative access to the Mount Robertson loop and summit tracks.

trails.name: Wharite Peak Track
trails.why: This track to the southern tip of the Ruahine Range is recommended for experienced trampers.

trails.name: Waiuta Town Walk
trails.why: Explore Waiuta, one of the West Coast’s best known ghost towns.

trails.name: Whakanui Track
trails.why: This track leads from Wainuiomata to the Ōrongorongo River and offers views of the Remutaka Range and surrounding areas.

trails.name: Lake Peel Track
trails.why: Walk to Salisbury Lodge via the beautiful Lake Peel. There are several huts along the way and Lake Peel is a good day walk destination.

trails.name: Glacier Burn Track
trails.why: This tramping track provides a route into Glacier Burn valley.

trails.name: Rockvale Track
trails.why: The northernmost access track to the Rock and Pillar Conservation Area.

trails.name: Mistake Creek Track
trails.why: This difficult tramping track leads from the Milford Road and up the Mistake Creek Valley through beech forest to the river flats.

trails.name: Te Iringa - Oamaru Track
trails.why: On this challenging and remote adventure ride, pass through beech forest and enjoy the scenery, streams and wildlife of the Kaimanawa Forest Park.

trails.name: Dore Pass Route
trails.why: This challenging tramping route leads from the Milford Road to Glade House on the Milford Track, via Dore Pass.

trails.name: Archer Track
trails.why: This walking and mountain biking track passes through native and pine forest from Penzance Bay to Elaine Bay.

trails.name: Dracophyllum Flat Track
trails.why: This track leads from Jacks Pass to Dracophyllum Flat, a popular picnic spot, then on to Texas Flat

trails.name: Mount Adams Route
trails.why: Mount Adams sits proudly on the edge of the Adams Wilderness Area in the Southern Alps/Kā Tiritiri o te Moana, and is a focal point for travellers along State Highway 6 from Lake Ianthe to Lake Wahapo.

trails.name: Ngamoko Track
trails.why: Walk along the Ngamoko Track as it steadily climbs to the Ngāmoko Range summit. You will be rewarded for your hard work by the views at the summit.

trails.name: Dusky Track - Loch Maree Hut to Lake Roe
trails.why: This difficult tramping track between Lake Hauroko and Lake Manapouri offers huge lakes, gushing rivers, vast forested valleys and lots of mud for experienced and well equipped trampers.

trails.name: Boyd Creek Walk
trails.why: This difficult tramping track leads from the Milford Road up the Boyd Creek onto the tops of the Countess Range, in the Snowdon Forest area.

trails.name: Patutu Route
trails.why: Climb to the summit of Patutu for great views of the coast and the North Island.

trails.name: Lotkow Road to Littles Clearing Track
trails.why: Lotkow Road branches off Whittle Road at the entry point to the Kaweka Forest Park.

trails.name: Hunt Saddle to Hunts Creek Hut Track
trails.why: Climb above a gorged section of river, follow a creek, and walk through native forest on the way to Hunts Creek Hut.

trails.name: Lake Hauroko Lookout Track
trails.why: This steep tramping track climbs from the edge of Lake Hauroko to a lookout with great views over the lake and nearby mountain ranges.

trails.name: Alborns Walk
trails.why: Walk through old mine workings on this well-graded loop track.

trails.name: Black Jack Track
trails.why: A loop track in Pukatea/Whites Bay with views of Cook Strait.

trails.name: Sanctuary Loop Walk
trails.why: The Sanctuary Track is an easy loop track that goes through remnant podocarp forest. You can also walk it at night as the Whirinaki Night Life Walk.

trails.name: Kiko Loop Track
trails.why: This short loop track is a great way for walkers and mountain bikers to experience the variety of nature in the Kaimanawa Forest Park.

trails.name: Speargrass Track
trails.why: For a good family challenge, walk to Speargrass Hut on an intermediate grade track.

trails.name: Neill Forks Hut to Maungahuka Hut Track
trails.why: This track links Neill Forks Hut with the Maungahuka Summit, via Concertina Knob.

trails.name: Buckland Peaks Route
trails.why: Walk through forest and subalpine scrub to Buckland Peaks for stunning views of the Paparoa Range.

trails.name: Cockayne Alley Track
trails.why: This track links Dracophyllum Flat Track with Cheeseman Road.

trails.name: Kea Basin Track
trails.why: It takes half a day to climb to this beautiful sub-alpine tussock basin beneath Mt Earnslaw/Pikirakatahi.

trails.name: Opouri Bridle Track
trails.why: Walk or mountain bike through native forest and farmland from Opouri Saddle down to Harvey Bay.

trails.name: Lewis Tops Track
trails.why: Climb to the open tops with superb views and picturesque tarns.

trails.name: Mount Fox Route
trails.why: Mount Fox Route is just 3 km south of the town of Fox Glacier. The challenging climb to the top is only suitable for experienced and properly equipped trampers.

trails.name: Woolshed Hill Track
trails.why: A steep climb on Woolshed Hill, with excellent views over the Waimakariri and Hawdon Valleys.

trails.name: Wairere Falls Track
trails.why: Wairere Falls Track weaves its way through moss covered rocks and tree roots. Large round boulders form natural pools and cascading waterfalls.

trails.name: Chummies Track
trails.why: Chummies Track is a steep climb up to John Reid Hut. It fords the Wangapeka River which is impassable if running high.

trails.name: Pass Creek Track
trails.why: This difficult tramping track leads from the Hollyford Road up to Lake Howden on the Routeburn Track.

trails.name: Avoca Valley Track
trails.why: This track leads from the Haper Valley up Avoca Valley to Avoca Hut.

trails.name: Middle Ridge Track
trails.why: This walking track links up with two popular tracks within Catchpool Valley.

trails.name: Wakamarina - Devils Creek Hut to Foster' Track
trails.why: Follow in the footsteps of old goldminers on the Wakamarina Track to cross the Richmond Range from the Wairau Valley to the Wakamarina Valley.

trails.name: Cattle Ridge Track
trails.why: This track gives outstanding views of the Remutaka Range and Ōrongorongo Valley.

trails.name: Wakamarina - Wakamarina Roadend to Devil Track
trails.why: Follow in the footsteps of old goldminers on the Wakamarina Track to cross the Richmond Range from the Wairau Valley to the Wakamarina Valley.

trails.name: Mount Tuhua Track - Upper Section
trails.why: This is a steep tramp to the open tussock peak of Mt. Tuhua and is suitable for fit people only.

trails.name: Ellis Basin Route
trails.why: Enjoy extensive views of the Ellis Basin and the surrounding mountains on this track to Ellis Hut.

trails.name: Pakihi Track - Pakihi Hut to Pakihi Roadend
trails.why: Pakihi Walk climbs through kamahi and rimu forest to a platform lookout.

trails.name: Peak Hill Track
trails.why: The climb to the top of Peak Hill rewards walkers with sweeping views of Lake Coleridge and its surrounds.

trails.name: Heaphy - Kohaihai to Scotts Beach Track
trails.why: Travel through expansive tussock downs, lush forests and nīkau palms to the roaring seas of the West Coast.

trails.name: Jollie Brook Circuit Track
trails.why: The Jollie Brook Circuit starts and finishes off Lake Sumner Road. There are many river crossings.

trails.name: Greta Track
trails.why: Pass by fellfields and short rock bluffs above Gretas Stream. This track is close to Lake Ōhau.

trails.name: Sparrowhawk Track
trails.why: The track follows a river then passes through the beech forest up the spur before reaching the Sparrowhawk Bivvy.

trails.name: Hawdon Hut Track
trails.why: A good introduction to backcountry tramping with multiple river crossings. This is a suitable trip for families if the river is not too high.

trails.name: Murray Creek Track
trails.why: Walk or mountain bike this loop walk through beech forest and historic goldfields.

trails.name: Stanfield Hut to Cattle Creek Hut Track
trails.why: A varied walk between two huts through a mixture of river, bush and ridgeline.

trails.name: Craigieburn Edge Track
trails.why: This track follows the Craigieburn Valley through mountain beech forest and tussock. It is best walked in summer and early autumn, as there can be avalanches when snow is present on the hills.

trails.name: Mount Robertson Loop Route
trails.why: Mountain bike or walk through mature and regenerating forest, with the option to visit the Mt Robertson/Tokomaru summit.

trails.name: Davies Track
trails.why: Follow Davies Track to Patuhā Trig to get great views of the coastline and Taranaki Maunga.

trails.name: Mount Stokes Track
trails.why: This tramping track in Kenepuru Sound follows a ridge to the summit, the highest point in the Sounds.

trails.name: Brookdale Track
trails.why: A short access track from Rock Road to the Rock and Pillar Conservation Area.

trails.name: Woolshed Creek Hut Track
trails.why: Walk this track for a family-friendly overnight or day tramp to Woolshed Creek Hut, on one end of the Mt Somers Track.

trails.name: Poulter River Track
trails.why: Poulter River Track is the only mountain biking track in Arthur’s Pass National Park. It has great scenery, some challenges and a good hut for an overnight stay.

trails.name: Lucretia Hut Route
trails.why: From the Nina Valley Track, follow Lucretia Hut Route to get to Lucretia Hut.

trails.name: Blue Valley Track
trails.why: The track to Camp Flat is easily accessible and an interesting day trip. You can continue on for another 13 km to the head of the valley.

trails.name: Waimoku Track
trails.why: Walk Waimoku Track in the Kaitake Range up to Patuhā Trig for great views along the coast and up to Taranaki Maunga.

trails.name: Shotover Saddle Route
trails.why: The Shotover Saddle Route offers magnificent views of the West Matukituki and Rob Roy valleys.

trails.name: Blue Range Hut to Cow Creek Hut Track
trails.why: A backcountry tramping track that joins Blue Range with Cow Creek Hut and the Waingawa River valley.

trails.name: Three Mile Stream Route
trails.why: The track runs from Hurunui swing bridge to Hope Kiwi Lodge. The route cuts down to join Hope Kiwi Track.

trails.name: Te Maire Loop Track
trails.why: Walk through a fine example of the podocarp forest that once covered much of the central North Island.

trails.name: Mckerrow Track
trails.why: Get panoramic views of Wainuiomata and the Hutt Valley as you climb to the top of Mt McKerrow.

trails.name: Tui Mine - Te Aroha Track
trails.why: A longer track from Te Aroha town to the summit of Te Aroha, via the historic Tui Mine.

trails.name: Te Kiekie Route
trails.why: This route links the summit of Mount Somers with the Mount Somers Track on the north side of the mountain.

trails.name: Bealey Spur Track
trails.why: Experience stunning views in fine weather from a more gradual track than most alpine tracks around Arthur's Pass village.

trails.name: Whakapapaiti Valley Track
trails.why: Winding through stunted beech forest, the Whakapapaiti Valley Track makes its way to the Whakapapaiti Hut.

trails.name: Camp Saddle Track
trails.why: An access track leads to Camp Saddle. From here, experienced backcountry trampers can explore untracked terrain.

trails.name: Roaring Stag Track
trails.why: Tramp from Putara Road end over a ridge and into the Ruamahanga Valley, to Roaring Stag Hut.

trails.name: Otamatapaio River Easement Track
trails.why: This easement leads to Manuherkia hunting area and Otamatapaio Hut.

trails.name: Temple Basin Track
trails.why: A nature photographer’s dream, experience expansive mountain views and alpine birdlife on this track to Temple Basin.

trails.name: Broken River Coal Mine Track
trails.why: This is a scenic walk with open views, following the route of a historic coal mine tramline.

trails.name: Mitre Peak Track
trails.why: Tramp from Mitre Flats to the bush line of Pukeamoamo/Mitre Peak.

trails.name: Hope Kiwi Track
trails.why: The track goes from the Hurunui swing bridge to Windy Point, and on to Hope Kiwi Lodge. This track is part of Te Araroa Trail.

trails.name: March Creek Track
trails.why: An access track leading from McKinnon Road to the Rock and Pillar Conservation Area.

trails.name: Deerford Loop
trails.why: Walk Deerford Loop Track to picturesque Makiekie Creek for a picnic and a paddle.

trails.name: Waiuta to Big River Track
trails.why: Walk or mountain bike an old benched pack track past old mining sites to Big River Hut.

trails.name: Mystery Lake Track
trails.why: The area around Mystery Lake has steep rocky ‘knobs’ smoothed by passing glaciers, jumbled scree and large Hall’s tōtara.

trails.name: West Matukituki Track
trails.why: Following the river and with views of notable glaciers, the West Matukituki Valley track takes you through sections of open farmland, native forest, and grassy flats before finishing at the head of the valley.

trails.name: Nina Valley Track - Sh7 to Nina Bivy
trails.why: This track goes to the upper Nina Valley. While relatively flat, this track can be rough and muddy in places and has several stream crossings.

trails.name: Moraine Creek Route
trails.why: This challenging tramping route leads up the Moraine Creek from the Hollyford Road to beautiful Lake Adelaide in an impressive glacial basin.

trails.name: Cable Bay Walkway
trails.why: Enjoy the coastal views on this walkway between Rotokura/Cable Bay and The Glen, near Nelson.

trails.name: Clay Ridge Track
trails.why: Climb up to Mt McKerrow for a great view of Wellington harbour and the surrounding hills near the top.

trails.name: Eldrig Peak Track
trails.why: This quite steep and difficult tramping track leads from the Borland Road through beech forest then into the tops where you can enjoy gorgeous views of Fiordland.

trails.name: Cascade Saddle Track - Asp Hut to Bush Edge
trails.why: The Cascade Saddle Route is an alpine crossing recommended for experienced trampers as a fine weather, summer route.

trails.name: Dover Route
trails.why: On a clear day this challenging route offers spectacular views of Taranaki Maunga and the coastline.
